newsitem.title: USA: More than 100 trapped after Philadelpha robbery try.
newsitem.headline: More than 100 trapped after Philadelpha robbery try.

text.p: More than 100 people were freed after being trapped inside a check-cashing business for hours on Friday after a botched robbery attempt in northeast Philadelphia, police said.
The drama -- which began Thursday evening with the kidnapping of the store's assistant manager, her husband and a clerk -- ended without serious injury Friday afternoon.

At least five suspects were involved, Philadelphia Police Commissioner Richard Neal told reporters after the incident. "We're not sure at this time how many more people were involved in this," Neal said.
Two people were arrested, away from the building, in connection with the incident and two others at the scene were detained for questioning.

A police spokesman, Cpl. Jim Pauley, said the incident had been treated as a hostage situation, although there were no negotiations with any hostage takers and it was police who had secured the building to prevent people from leaving.
"Based on the information received at the time, they were considered hostages," Pauley said.

A Philadelphia police officer accidentally shot himself in the hand in the course of the incident and a pregnant woman was reported to have been taken to the hospital. No other injuries were reported.

Neal said the incident began Thursday when the assistant manager of the Financial Exchange, where individuals can cash checks and pick up food stamps and welfare checks, was kidnapped along with her husband and an exchange clerk.
The three were taken to the assistant manager's home and held at gunpoint with her family.
Four men conducted the kidnapping and a fifth was waiting at the home. A security guard from the business was later brought to the home, and his uniform was taken by the robbers, Neal said.

The assistant manager was then brought to the business early Friday morning, accompanied by one of the robbers in the security guard's uniform, in an attempt to gain entrance and apparently rob an armoured car, he said.
However, the armoured car did not linger at the site and the robbery was stymied, Neal said.

Neal said the assistant manager escaped the building at about 10:30 a.m. Shortly thereafter, police nearby stopped a car and three men jumped out, one pointing an automatic weapon at police. After an exchange of gunfire, one man was arrested and two fled. Police believe the three were involved in the robbery attempt.
Pauley said as police learned of the incident they promptly surrounded the building.
A clerk inside, communicating with police negotiators, had said some remaining inside the building were acting suspiciously, which fuelled concerns of a hostage situation, Neal said.

The police eventually allowed those inside -- including many women and children -- to slowly file out of the building. As they left, they were searched and questioned by police to find any robbers who may have tried to blend in.
They were then transported by police to a site where they were to be interviewed.
